diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: Scope follows source structure
sections.body: JavaScript resolves a name by looking in the current lexical environment and then outward through enclosing environments. The lookup depends on where a function is defined, not where it is later called. This is why a nested function can use its parent function’s variables.

sections.title: A function remembers outer bindings
sections.body: A closure is a function together with access to the lexical environment where it was created. If the inner function survives after the outer function returns, those needed bindings remain reachable. The binding is remembered, so later updates can be observed; it is not merely a frozen copy of the first value.

sections.title: Practical closures
sections.body: A factory can return a function configured with a value, or keep state that callers can change only through returned methods. Event handlers and React callbacks are closures too. This power is useful, but captured values can become stale when a framework reruns code and an old callback remains active.

sections.title: Closures affect lifetime
sections.body: A closure can keep referenced data alive. Long-lived timers, listeners, or caches may therefore retain more memory than expected. Remove listeners and timers when their work ends, and capture only the data the callback truly needs.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Closures and lexical scope is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using closures and lexical scope behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.

interviewQuestions.question: Where can closures and lexical scope affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.
